narrative:
Based on your profile, the model estimates a 14% chance that you might not pass your final year. Because this is above the 10% threshold, you are required to take additional remedial courses to help ensure your success.

The prediction was shaped most strongly by three aspects of your background. First, your record shows no previous class failures, which is a very positive sign and actually reduced your risk compared to others. Most students in your situation also have no past failures, and this similarity worked in your favor. Second, your strong desire to pursue higher education also helped lower your risk. Every student in your group shares this ambition, and it signals motivation and future goals, which the model sees as protective. Third, your mother’s education level is in the 5th to 9th grade range, which is less common among students who are not required to take remedial courses—half of those students have mothers with higher education. This factor slightly increased your risk, as students whose parents have more education tend to have a lower chance of failing.

Although two of the most important factors worked in your favor, the overall combination of your background and school record led to a prediction above the threshold. Taking remedial courses is a proactive step to give you extra support and maximize your chances of passing. Use this opportunity to strengthen your skills and address any challenges early, so you can achieve your academic goals.
